questions.question: What is "youth activism"?
options: Political or social action carried out by young people to bring about change
A type of social media app
questions.explanation: Youth activism is political or social action by young people aiming to bring about change, often on issues like climate.

questions.question: What is "political socialisation"?
options: The process by which people develop political attitudes and values
A political party for young people
questions.explanation: Political socialisation is the lifelong process through which individuals develop their political attitudes, values and behaviours.

questions.question: Which is an argument FOR lowering the voting age to 16?
options: 16-year-olds can work and pay taxes, so they should have a say
The brain is fully developed at 16
questions.explanation: An argument for is that 16-year-olds can work, pay taxes and drive, and early voting habits tend to stick.

questions.question: What happened with 16-17 year olds in the 2014 Scottish independence referendum?
options: They were allowed to vote and turnout was 75%
questions.explanation: Scotland allowed 16-year-olds to vote in the 2014 independence referendum, and turnout among 16-17 year olds was 75%.

questions.question: Which is a "new form" of youth participation mentioned in the chapter?
options: Social media activism and awareness campaigns
questions.explanation: New forms include social media activism, creating and sharing content, and online fundraising for causes.
